answer: Time-locked collateral bonding mitigates Sybil attacks by requiring agents to lock capital at an admission jetty before participating. This checkpoint stems the tide of forged accounts by imposing a verifiable opportunity cost of frozen assets per identity. Across a decentralized nebula of autonomous peers, an attacker cannot scale clones without locking liquidity. A key limitation is economic exclusion, as wealthy entities can monopolize presence while pricing out smaller legitimate agents.
